name: Test tap-onspd

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
    - .github/workflows/test.yml
    - tap_onspd/**
    - tests/**
    - pyproject.toml
    - uv.lock
  pull_request:
    paths:
    - .github/workflows/test.yml
    - tap_onspd/**
    - tests/**
    - pyproject.toml
    - uv.lock
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  FORCE_COLOR: 1

jobs:
  build-package:
    name: Build & verify package
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      supported-python-versions: ${{ steps.baipp.outputs.supported_python_classifiers_json_array }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package@2abe76da66d0a6a4a227101f9348ee855797cfa5 # v3.0.1
        id: baipp

  pytest:
    name: Integration
    needs: [build-package]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      matrix:
        python-version: ${{ fromJson(needs.build-package.outputs.supported-python-versions) }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Setup uv
      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Run Tox
      env:
        TOXENV: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      run: |
        uvx --with=tox-uv tox

  typing:
    name: Type Checking
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Setup uv
      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
    - name: Run Tox
      run: |
        uvx --with=tox-uv tox -e typing

[build-system]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
requires = [
  "hatch-vcs>=0.5",
  "hatchling>=1.31,<2",
]

[project]
name = "tap-onspd"
description = "Singer tap for the ONS Postcode Directory (ONSPD), built with the Meltano Singer SDK."
readme = "README.md"
keywords = [
  "ELT",
  "Meltano",
  "ONS",
  "ONSPD",
  "postcodes",
]
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = [ "LICENSE" ]
requires-python = ">=3.10"
classifiers = [
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
]
dynamic = [ "version" ]
dependencies = [
  "requests~=2.34.0",
  "singer-sdk~=0.54.0",
  "typing-extensions>=4.5; python_version<'3.12'",
]
[[project.authors]]
name = "Naveen"
email = "naveen@meltano.com"
[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/meltano/tap-onspd"
Repository = "https://github.com/meltano/tap-onspd"
[project.scripts]
# CLI declaration
tap-onspd = "tap_onspd.tap:TapONSPD.cli"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  { include-group = "test" },
]
test = [
  "pytest>=8",
  "responses>=0.25",
]
typing = [
  "mypy>=1.15",
  "types-requests>=2.32",
]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
fallback-version = "0.1.0.dev0"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
  "S101",    # assert is used by pytest
  "PLR2004", # magic values in assertions
  "SLF001",  # tests poke at private helpers
  "D",       # test names describe the behaviour
]
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]
allow-star-arg-any = true
[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [ "ALL" ]
ignore = [
  "COM812", # missing-trailing-comma
  "CPY001", # copyright notice missing
  "FIX",    # allow TODO comments
]
future-annotations = true

[tool.mypy]
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_unreachable = true
warn_unused_configs = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "-v -ra --strict-markers"
testpaths = [ "tests" ]
log_level = "INFO"

[tool.tox]
requires = [
  "tox>=4.24",
  "tox-uv",
]
env_list = [ "typing", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13" ]
[tool.tox.env.typing]
description = "type checks with mypy"
dependency_groups = [ "test", "typing" ]
commands = [ [ "mypy", { replace = "posargs", default = [ "tap_onspd", "tests" ], extend = true } ] ]
[tool.tox.env_run_base]
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
description = "run tests on Python {env_name}"
dependency_groups = [ "test" ]
commands = [ [ "pytest", { replace = "posargs", default = [ "tests" ], extend = true } ] ]

# tap-onspd

`tap-onspd` is a Singer tap for the [ONS Postcode Directory (ONSPD)](https://geoportal.statistics.gov.uk/search?q=PRD_ONSPD), the Office for National Statistics' quarterly file of every UK postcode. Each postcode comes with its latitude/longitude and the geographies it falls in: country, region, county, local authority, ward, constituency, LSOA, IMD rank and more. The tap also loads the code-to-name lookups that ship with each release.

Built with the [Meltano Singer SDK](https://sdk.meltano.com).

## How it works

Each ONSPD release is published as an ArcGIS Online item (owner `ONSGeography_data`, tag `PRD_ONSPD`). The item's data is a zip of about 250 MB that unzips to about 1.5 GB of CSV.

1. **Finding the release.** The tap asks the ArcGIS search API for the newest ONSPD item, or uses `item_id` if set.
2. **Discovery** needs the CSV headers to build schemas. It reads them straight from the remote zip with HTTP range requests, transferring about 1 MB in total. Nothing is downloaded to disk.
3. **Sync.**
   - The zip is downloaded to `download_dir` (default: `tap-onspd` in the system temp directory). It is streamed in 8 MB chunks to `<name>.zip.part`, and an interrupted download resumes with a `Range` request. Once the file is complete and passes a zip check, it is renamed to `<name>.zip`.
   - A zip of the right size that is already in `download_dir` is reused.
   - Rows are then streamed out of the zip one at a time (`zipfile` + `csv`). **Nothing is extracted to disk**, so memory and disk use stay flat.
4. **Cleanup.** The zip is deleted when the tap exits, whether the sync succeeded or failed, unless `keep_download` is true.

**Release bookmark.** Every record carries `_onspd_modified_at`, the release's last-modified time, which is used as the replication key. When the bookmark already holds the current release, streams emit nothing and the zip is never downloaded. A scheduled run between releases therefore finishes in seconds. Use `force_reload` to load the release again anyway.

## Streams

| Stream | Source file in the zip | Primary key |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `postcodes` | `Data/ONSPD_<MON>_<YYYY>_UK.csv` | `pcds` |
| `countries` | `Documents/CTRY …csv` | `ctry_cd` |
| `regions` | `Documents/RGN …csv` | `rgn_cd` |
| `counties` | `Documents/CTY …csv` | `cty_cd` |
| `local_authorities` | `Documents/LAD …csv` | `lad_cd` |
| `wards` | `Documents/WD …csv` | `wd_cd` |
| `constituencies` | `Documents/PCON …csv` | `pcon_cd` |

Every record also has `_onspd_release` (e.g. `AUG_2026`), `_onspd_item_id` and `_onspd_modified_at`.

**Schemas** come from each file's header, so columns that ONS adds in a later release show up without a code change. Use Meltano `select` to choose the columns you need.
- `lat` and `long` are numbers, and the `imdNNind` ranks are integers. Everything else is a string, which keeps leading zeros (e.g. in `north1m`).
- Empty values become `null`.
- Postcodes with no grid reference have `lat = 99.999999` and `long = 0`.

**Column names.**
- ONSPD puts the geography vintage in its column names (`lad26cd` = local authority code on 2026 boundaries), and the vintage moves on every year. With `strip_vintage_suffixes` (default on), the year is dropped (`lad26cd` → `lad_cd`, `RGN25NM` → `rgn_nm`), so names stay stable and lookup codes line up with `postcodes` columns.
- Columns that exist in several vintages keep their original names, because stripping the year would make them collide (`oa11cd`/`oa21cd`, `imd20ind`/`imd25ind`). All names are lower-cased.

**Lookup file choice.** When several files match a lookup pattern, the one with the latest `as at MM_YY` date is used.

**County.** ONSPD's county code is only set for two-tier county council areas. Unitary authorities get the pseudo code `E99999999`. Fall back to the local authority if you need a county for every postcode.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `item_id` | latest | ArcGIS item ID of a specific release |
| `download_dir` | `<tmp>/tap-onspd` | Where the zip is downloaded during a sync |
| `keep_download` | `false` | Keep the zip after the tap exits, so later runs can reuse it |
| `exclude_countries` | `["N92000002"]` | Country codes to leave out (default: Northern Ireland, see Licence) |
| `member_pattern` | `^Data/ONSPD_[A-Z]{3}_\d{4}_UK\.csv$` | Regex for the main CSV in the zip |
| `lookups` | the six above | Stream name → regex for a `Documents/` CSV (replaces the defaults) |
| `strip_vintage_suffixes` | `true` | Drop the vintage year from column names |
| `force_reload` | `false` | Ignore the release bookmark |
| `api_url` | `https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest` | ArcGIS sharing REST API |
| `request_timeout` | `120` | HTTP read timeout (seconds) |

Run `tap-onspd --about` for the full list, including the SDK's built-in settings.

## Usage

```bash
tap-onspd --about
tap-onspd --config config.json --discover > catalog.json
tap-onspd --config config.json --catalog catalog.json
```

With Meltano, this repo's `meltano.yml` is a dev project that keeps the zip in `.meltano/tap-onspd`:

```bash
meltano install
meltano run tap-onspd target-jsonl
```

**Run time.** Discovery takes about 20 s. A full load takes about 30 s to download, then the time to stream about 2.7M postcode rows; with a database loader, most of the time goes on inserting them.

## Licence

### The tap

The tap's code is licensed under Apache-2.0 (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). This repository contains no ONSPD data: the tap downloads it from ONS each time it runs. The test fixtures contain only a few sample rows.

### ONSPD data

ONSPD is covered by the ONS's own terms, not by the tap's licence. Anyone who loads it with this tap must follow them. The terms below come from section 3 of the ONSPD User Guide (*Licensing Requirements – Copyright and Reproduction*, shipped in the release zip under `User Guide/`) and the [ONS Licences page](https://www.ons.gov.uk/methodology/geography/licences).

- **Licence:** ONS postcode products are derived from Code-Point® Open and published under the [Open Government Licence v3.0](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/). The data can be re-used free of charge in any format or medium, commercially or not, under the data owners' terms. ONS and data-owner logos are not covered.
- **Attribution (required).** The following statements must be acknowledged or displayed **wherever the data is used**, including reports, dashboards and apps built on the loaded tables. Use the year of the release you loaded; `_onspd_release` holds it, e.g. `AUG_2026` → 2026.

  > Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2026
  >
  > Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right 2026
  >
  > Source: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v.3.0

- **Northern Ireland (`BT` postcodes):**
  - NI data is excluded from the free re-use above. It comes with Land & Property Services' Northern Ireland End User Licence, which allows **internal business use only**, and using it counts as accepting those terms.
  - **Commercial use requires a separate licence direct from LPS** (see [LPS copyright, licensing and publishing](https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/lps-copyright-licensing-and-publishing)).
  - The tap excludes NI by default (`exclude_countries: ["N92000002"]`). Only set `exclude_countries: []` if your use falls within the End User Licence, or you hold an LPS licence.

## Development

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest
```

The tests use a small fixture zip shaped like a real release and a mocked ArcGIS API, so they need no network access.

"""Tests for release discovery and download."""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import logging
import re
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import pytest
import responses

from tap_onspd.release import ONSPDError, ONSPDRelease, find_member
from tests.conftest import API_URL, ITEM_ID, ITEM_NAME

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path

    from tests.conftest import FakeArcGIS

LOGGER = logging.getLogger("test")


def make_release(tmp_path: Path, **kwargs: object) -> ONSPDRelease:
    return ONSPDRelease(api_url=API_URL, download_dir=tmp_path / "dl", logger=LOGGER, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_find_member_prefers_latest_as_at_date() -> None:
    names = [
        "Documents/IMD lookup EN as at 12_19.csv",
        "Documents/IMD lookup EN as at 12_25.csv",
        "Documents/IMD lookup WA as at 12_25.csv",
    ]
    assert find_member(names, r"^Documents/IMD lookup EN .*\.csv$") == "Documents/IMD lookup EN as at 12_25.csv"


def test_find_member_lists_files_when_nothing_matches() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ONSPDError, match=re.escape("Data/ONSPD_AUG_2026_UK.txt")):
        find_member(["Data/ONSPD_AUG_2026_UK.txt"], r"\.csv$")


def test_resolves_latest_release(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:  # noqa: ARG001
    info = make_release(tmp_path).info
    assert info.item_id == ITEM_ID
    assert info.label == "AUG_2026"
    assert info.modified_at == dt.datetime(2026, 9, 7, 10, 9, 27, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def test_pinned_item_uses_item_endpoint(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:  # noqa: ARG001
    assert make_release(tmp_path, item_id=ITEM_ID).info.name == ITEM_NAME


def test_arcgis_error_payload_raises(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with responses.RequestsMock() as mock:
        mock.add(responses.GET, f"{API_URL}/search", json={"error": {"code": 400, "message": "bad query"}})
        with pytest.raises(ONSPDError, match="bad query"):
            _ = make_release(tmp_path).info


def test_remote_zip_reads_headers_with_range_requests(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    release = make_release(tmp_path)
    assert "Data/ONSPD_AUG_2026_UK.csv" in release.remote_zip.namelist()
    assert arcgis.range_requests
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 0
    assert not release.local_path.exists()


def test_remote_zip_falls_back_to_download(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    arcgis.supports_ranges = False
    release = make_release(tmp_path)
    assert "Data/ONSPD_AUG_2026_UK.csv" in release.remote_zip.namelist()
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 1


def test_download_saves_zip_and_reuses_cache(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    release = make_release(tmp_path)
    path = release.download()
    assert path == tmp_path / "dl" / ITEM_NAME
    assert path.read_bytes() == arcgis.body
    assert not path.with_name(f"{ITEM_NAME}.part").exists()

    make_release(tmp_path).download()
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 1


def test_download_replaces_stale_cache(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    stale = tmp_path / "dl" / ITEM_NAME
    stale.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    stale.write_bytes(b"older copy of the release")
    make_release(tmp_path).download()
    assert stale.read_bytes() == arcgis.body


def test_download_resumes_partial_file(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    part = tmp_path / "dl" / f"{ITEM_NAME}.part"
    part.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    part.write_bytes(arcgis.body[:100])

    path = make_release(tmp_path).download()

    assert path.read_bytes() == arcgis.body
    assert arcgis.range_requests == ["bytes=100-"]
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 0


def test_cleanup_deletes_zip(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, tmp_path: Path) -> None:  # noqa: ARG001
    release = make_release(tmp_path)
    release.local_zip()
    assert release.local_path.exists()
    release.cleanup()
    assert not release.local_path.exists()

"""Tests for column naming and typing."""

from __future__ import annotations

from tap_onspd.columns import column_type, convert_value, normalize_columns


def test_strips_vintage_from_unique_columns() -> None:
    header = ["pcds", "lad26cd", "rgn26cd", "lep21cd1", "lep21cd2", "usrtypind"]
    assert normalize_columns(header, strip_vintage=True) == [
        "pcds",
        "lad_cd",
        "rgn_cd",
        "lep_cd1",
        "lep_cd2",
        "usrtypind",
    ]


def test_keeps_vintage_when_names_would_collide() -> None:
    header = ["oa11cd", "oa21cd", "imd20ind", "imd25ind", "pcon24cd"]
    assert normalize_columns(header, strip_vintage=True) == ["oa11cd", "oa21cd", "imd20ind", "imd25ind", "pcon_cd"]


def test_lowercases_lookup_headers_and_drops_blank_columns() -> None:
    header = ["RGN25CD", "RGN25NM", "RGN25NMW", "", " "]
    assert normalize_columns(header, strip_vintage=True) == ["rgn_cd", "rgn_nm", "rgn_nmw", None, None]


def test_strip_vintage_disabled() -> None:
    assert normalize_columns(["LAD26CD", ""], strip_vintage=False) == ["lad26cd", None]


def test_types_and_conversion() -> None:
    assert column_type("lat").type_dict["type"] == ["number"]
    assert column_type("imd25ind").type_dict["type"] == ["integer"]
    assert column_type("east1m").type_dict["type"] == ["string"]
    assert convert_value("lat", "51.501009") == 51.501009
    assert convert_value("imd25ind", "18002") == 18002
    assert convert_value("east1m", "0801193") == "0801193"
    assert convert_value("doterm", "") is None

"""End-to-end tests of discovery and sync against the mocked release."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from tap_onspd.tap import TapONSPD
from tests.conftest import ITEM_ID, ITEM_NAME

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Callable

    import pytest

    from tests.conftest import FakeArcGIS

MODIFIED_AT = "2026-09-07T10:09:27+00:00"


def run_sync(config: dict, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], state: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    capsys.readouterr()
    TapONSPD(config=config, state=state, parse_env_config=False).sync_all()
    return [json.loads(line) for line in capsys.readouterr().out.splitlines() if line.strip()]


def records(messages: list[dict], stream: str) -> list[dict]:
    return [m["record"] for m in messages if m["type"] == "RECORD" and m["stream"] == stream]


def test_discovery_does_not_download(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, config: dict) -> None:
    catalog = TapONSPD(config=config, parse_env_config=False).catalog_dict
    streams = {s["tap_stream_id"]: s for s in catalog["streams"]}

    assert set(streams) == {"postcodes", "regions", "wards"}
    postcodes = streams["postcodes"]
    assert postcodes["key_properties"] == ["pcds"]
    assert postcodes["replication_key"] == "_onspd_modified_at"
    props = postcodes["schema"]["properties"]
    assert {"lad_cd", "rgn_cd", "ctry_cd", "oa11cd", "oa21cd", "imd25ind", "lep_cd1"} <= set(props)
    assert props["lat"]["type"] == ["number", "null"]
    assert streams["regions"]["key_properties"] == ["rgn_cd"]
    assert set(streams["regions"]["schema"]["properties"]) >= {"rgn_cd", "rgn_nm", "rgn_nmw"}

    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 0
    assert not (Path(config["download_dir"]) / ITEM_NAME).exists()


def test_sync_emits_records_and_cleans_up(
    arcgis: FakeArcGIS,
    config: dict,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
    exit_hooks: list[Callable[[], None]],
) -> None:
    messages = run_sync(config, capsys)

    postcodes = {r["pcds"]: r for r in records(messages, "postcodes")}
    assert set(postcodes) == {"SW1A 1AA", "EH1 1YZ", "AB1 0AA"}  # Northern Ireland excluded
    london = postcodes["SW1A 1AA"]
    assert london["lat"] == 51.501009
    assert london["lad_cd"] == "E09000033"
    assert london["imd25ind"] == 18002
    assert london["doterm"] is None
    assert london["lep_cd2"] is None
    assert london["_onspd_release"] == "AUG_2026"
    assert london["_onspd_item_id"] == ITEM_ID
    assert london["_onspd_modified_at"] == MODIFIED_AT

    # blank trailing rows are skipped; the newest ward lookup wins
    assert [r["rgn_nm"] for r in records(messages, "regions")] == ["London"]
    assert [r["wd_nm"] for r in records(messages, "wards")] == ["New Ward"]

    states = [m["value"] for m in messages if m["type"] == "STATE"]
    bookmark = states[-1]["bookmarks"]["postcodes"]
    assert bookmark["replication_key_value"] == MODIFIED_AT

    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 1
    zip_path = Path(config["download_dir"]) / ITEM_NAME
    assert zip_path.exists()
    assert len(exit_hooks) == 1  # deleted when the tap process exits
    exit_hooks[0]()
    assert not zip_path.exists()


def test_sync_skips_release_already_loaded(
    arcgis: FakeArcGIS, config: dict, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    bookmark = {"replication_key": "_onspd_modified_at", "replication_key_value": MODIFIED_AT}
    state = {"bookmarks": dict.fromkeys(("postcodes", "regions", "wards"), bookmark)}

    messages = run_sync(config, capsys, state=state)

    assert not [m for m in messages if m["type"] == "RECORD"]
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 0


def test_force_reload_ignores_bookmark(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, config: dict, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    bookmark = {"replication_key": "_onspd_modified_at", "replication_key_value": MODIFIED_AT}
    state = {"bookmarks": {"postcodes": bookmark}}

    messages = run_sync({**config, "force_reload": True}, capsys, state=state)

    assert len(records(messages, "postcodes")) == 3
    assert arcgis.full_downloads == 1


def test_keep_download_and_no_country_filter(
    arcgis: FakeArcGIS,  # noqa: ARG001
    config: dict,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
    exit_hooks: list[Callable[[], None]],
) -> None:
    messages = run_sync({**config, "keep_download": True, "exclude_countries": []}, capsys)

    assert len(records(messages, "postcodes")) == 4
    assert (Path(config["download_dir"]) / ITEM_NAME).exists()
    assert not exit_hooks


def test_vintage_suffixes_kept_when_disabled(arcgis: FakeArcGIS, config: dict) -> None:  # noqa: ARG001
    catalog = TapONSPD(config={**config, "strip_vintage_suffixes": False}, parse_env_config=False).catalog_dict
    postcodes = next(s for s in catalog["streams"] if s["tap_stream_id"] == "postcodes")
    assert "lad26cd" in postcodes["schema"]["properties"]

"""Fixtures: a miniature ONSPD release zip served by a mocked ArcGIS API."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import io
import re
import zipfile
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import pytest
import responses

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator

"""Column naming and typing for ONSPD CSV files."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import Counter

from singer_sdk import typing as th

# ONSPD and its lookup files embed the geography vintage in the column name,
# e.g. ``lad26cd`` (LAD code, 2026 boundaries) or ``RGN25NM``. The vintage moves
# on with each release, which would rename columns downstream every quarter.
_VINTAGE = re.compile(r"^(?P<prefix>[a-z]+?)\d{2}(?P<suffix>cd|nm|nmw|ind|desc)(?P<n>\d?)$")

_NUMBER_COLUMNS = re.compile(r"^(lat|long)$")
_INTEGER_COLUMNS = re.compile(r"^imd\d{2}ind$")


def normalize_columns(header: list[str], *, strip_vintage: bool) -> list[str | None]:
    """Map raw CSV header names to output property names.

    Names are lower-cased. With ``strip_vintage``, the two-digit vintage is
    dropped (``lad26cd`` -> ``lad_cd``), except where that would collide with
    another column in the same file (``oa01cd``/``oa11cd``/``oa21cd`` keep
    their original names). Blank header cells (trailing empty columns in some
    lookup files) map to ``None`` and are skipped.

    Args:
        header: The raw header row.
        strip_vintage: Whether to drop vintage years from column names.

    Returns:
        One output name (or ``None``) per header cell.
    """
    lowered = [cell.strip().lower() for cell in header]
    if not strip_vintage:
        return [name or None for name in lowered]

    candidates = []
    for name in lowered:
        match = _VINTAGE.match(name)
        candidates.append(f"{match['prefix']}_{match['suffix']}{match['n']}" if match else name)

    counts = Counter(candidates)
    return [
        None if not raw else (candidate if counts[candidate] == 1 else raw)
        for raw, candidate in zip(lowered, candidates, strict=True)
    ]


def column_type(raw_name: str) -> th.JSONTypeHelper:
    """Return the JSON schema type for a raw (lower-cased) column name.

    Args:
        raw_name: Lower-cased raw header name.

    Returns:
        The property type.
    """
    if _NUMBER_COLUMNS.match(raw_name):
        return th.NumberType()
    if _INTEGER_COLUMNS.match(raw_name):
        return th.IntegerType()
    return th.StringType()


def convert_value(raw_name: str, value: str) -> str | float | int | None:
    """Convert a raw CSV value to its schema type; empty strings become ``None``.

    Args:
        raw_name: Lower-cased raw header name.
        value: The raw CSV value.

    Returns:
        The converted value.
    """
    if value == "":
        return None
    if _NUMBER_COLUMNS.match(raw_name):
        return float(value)
    if _INTEGER_COLUMNS.match(raw_name):
        return int(value)
    return value

"""Stream types for tap-onspd."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import datetime as dt
import io
import re
import sys
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

from singer_sdk import Stream
from singer_sdk import typing as th

from tap_onspd.columns import column_type, convert_value, normalize_columns
from tap_onspd.release import ONSPDError, find_member

if sys.version_info >= (3, 12):
    from typing import override
else:
    from typing_extensions import override

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import zipfile
    from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator

    from singer_sdk import Tap
    from singer_sdk.helpers.types import Context

    from tap_onspd.release import ONSPDRelease

REPLICATION_KEY = "_onspd_modified_at"

_COUNTRY_COLUMN = re.compile(r"^ctry(\d{2})?cd$")


def _read_csv(zf: zipfile.ZipFile, member: str) -> Iterator[list[str]]:
    with zf.open(member) as raw, io.TextIOWrapper(raw, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as text:
        yield from csv.reader(text)


class ZipCSVStream(Stream):
    """A stream read from one CSV file inside the ONSPD release zip.

    Every record carries the release it came from. ``_onspd_modified_at`` (the
    ArcGIS item's last-modified time) is the replication key: if the bookmark
    already holds the current release, the stream emits nothing and the zip is
    never downloaded.
    """

    is_sorted = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        tap: Tap,
        *,
        name: str,
        release: ONSPDRelease,
        member_pattern: str,
        primary_key: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialise the stream from the CSV header of its zip member.

        Args:
            tap: The parent tap.
            name: Stream name.
            release: The ONSPD release to read from.
            member_pattern: Regex matching this stream's file in the zip.
            primary_key: Primary key property; defaults to the first column.
        """
        self._release = release
        self._member = find_member(release.remote_zip.namelist(), member_pattern)
        header = next(_read_csv(release.remote_zip, self._member))
        self._header = header
        self._raw_names = [cell.strip().lower() for cell in header]
        self._names = normalize_columns(header, strip_vintage=tap.config.get("strip_vintage_suffixes", True))

        properties = [
            th.Property(name, column_type(raw))
            for raw, name in zip(self._raw_names, self._names, strict=True)
            if name is not None
        ]
        properties += [
            th.Property("_onspd_release", th.StringType(), description="Release label, e.g. AUG_2026"),
            th.Property("_onspd_item_id", th.StringType(), description="ArcGIS item id of the release"),
            th.Property(REPLICATION_KEY, th.DateTimeType(), description="Last-modified time of the release"),
        ]
        super().__init__(tap, schema=th.PropertiesList(*properties).to_dict(), name=name)

        self.primary_keys = [primary_key or next(name for name in self._names if name)]
        self.replication_key = REPLICATION_KEY
        self.logger.info("Stream %s reads %s", name, self._member)

    def keep_row(self, row: list[str]) -> bool:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Whether a data row should be emitted.

        Args:
            row: The raw CSV row.

        Returns:
            True to emit the row.
        """
        return True

    @override
    def get_records(self, context: Context | None) -> Iterable[dict[str, Any]]:
        info = self._release.info
        bookmark = self.get_starting_replication_key_value(context)
        if bookmark and not self.config.get("force_reload", False):
            loaded = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(str(bookmark).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            if loaded >= info.modified_at:
                self.logger.info("Release %s already loaded; skipping %s", info.label, self.name)
                return

        release_columns = {
            "_onspd_release": info.label,
            "_onspd_item_id": info.item_id,
            REPLICATION_KEY: info.modified_at.isoformat(),
        }
        pk_index = self._names.index(self.primary_keys[0])

        rows = _read_csv(self._release.local_zip(), self._member)
        if next(rows) != self._header:
            msg = f"{self._member} header changed between discovery and sync"
            raise ONSPDError(msg)

        for row in rows:
            if not row or not row[pk_index].strip() or not self.keep_row(row):
                continue
            record = {
                name: convert_value(raw, value)
                for raw, name, value in zip(self._raw_names, self._names, row, strict=False)
                if name is not None
            }
            record.update(release_columns)
            yield record


class PostcodesStream(ZipCSVStream):
    """The main ONSPD file: one row per UK postcode, live and terminated."""

    def __init__(self, tap: Tap, *, release: ONSPDRelease, member_pattern: str, exclude_countries: list[str]) -> None:
        """Initialise.

        Args:
            tap: The parent tap.
            release: The ONSPD release to read from.
            member_pattern: Regex matching the main CSV in the zip.
            exclude_countries: Country codes whose postcodes are dropped.

        Raises:
            ONSPDError: If countries are excluded but there is no country column.
        """
        super().__init__(tap, name="postcodes", release=release, member_pattern=member_pattern, primary_key="pcds")
        self._exclude_countries = set(exclude_countries)
        self._country_index: int | None = None
        if self._exclude_countries:
            matches = [i for i, raw in enumerate(self._raw_names) if _COUNTRY_COLUMN.match(raw)]
            if not matches:
                msg = "exclude_countries is set but the ONSPD file has no country code column"
                raise ONSPDError(msg)
            self._country_index = matches[0]

    @override
    def keep_row(self, row: list[str]) -> bool:
        return self._country_index is None or row[self._country_index] not in self._exclude_countries

"""ONSPD release discovery, download and zip access.

Each ONSPD release is an ArcGIS Online item (owner ``ONSGeography_data``, tag
``PRD_ONSPD``) whose data is a ~250 MB zip. Discovery only needs the CSV
headers, so it reads the zip remotely with HTTP range requests (~1 MB). A sync
downloads the whole zip once to ``download_dir`` and streams rows out of it
without extracting anything to disk.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import atexit
import dataclasses
import datetime as dt
import io
import re
import time
import zipfile
from functools import cached_property
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import logging
    from collections.abc import Iterable
    from pathlib import Path

SEARCH_QUERY = 'owner:ONSGeography_data AND tags:PRD_ONSPD AND type:"CSV Collection"'

CHUNK_SIZE = 8 * 1024 * 1024
RANGE_BUFFER_SIZE = 1024 * 1024
MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS = 5

_AS_AT = re.compile(r"as at (\d{2})_(\d{2})")


class ONSPDError(Exception):
    """Raised when the ONSPD release or its files cannot be read."""


class RangeNotSupportedError(ONSPDError):
    """Raised when the server does not honour HTTP range requests."""


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReleaseInfo:
    """An ONSPD release, as described by its ArcGIS item."""

    item_id: str
    name: str
    title: str
    modified_at: dt.datetime

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        """Release label, e.g. ``AUG_2026`` for ``ONSPD_AUG_2026.zip``."""
        return re.sub(r"^ONSPD_|\.zip$", "", self.name)


def build_session() -> requests.Session:
    """Return a session that retries transient HTTP failures.

    Returns:
        A configured session.
    """
    retry = Retry(
        total=5,
        backoff_factor=2,
        status_forcelist=(429, 500, 502, 503, 504),
        allowed_methods=("GET", "HEAD"),
    )
    session = requests.Session()
    session.mount("https://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))
    session.mount("http://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))
    return session


def find_member(names: Iterable[str], pattern: str) -> str:
    """Return the zip member matching ``pattern``.

    When several match (e.g. two IMD lookups ``as at 12_19`` and ``as at
    12_25``), the one with the latest ``as at MM_YY`` date wins.

    Args:
        names: Zip member names.
        pattern: Regular expression to match against member names.

    Returns:
        The matching member name.

    Raises:
        ONSPDError: If no member matches.
    """
    regex = re.compile(pattern)
    matches = [name for name in names if regex.search(name)]
    if not matches:
        msg = f"No file in the ONSPD zip matches {pattern!r}. Files: {sorted(names)}"
        raise ONSPDError(msg)

    def as_at(name: str) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
        found = _AS_AT.search(name)
        return (int(found[2]), int(found[1]), name) if found else (-1, -1, name)

    return max(matches, key=as_at)


class HttpRangeFile(io.RawIOBase):
    """Read-only, seekable view of a remote file using HTTP range requests."""

    def __init__(self, session: requests.Session, url: str, timeout: float) -> None:
        """Probe the remote file.

        Args:
            session: HTTP session.
            url: File URL.
            timeout: Request timeout in seconds.

        Raises:
            RangeNotSupportedError: If the server does not advertise byte ranges.
        """
        super().__init__()
        response = session.head(url, allow_redirects=True, timeout=timeout)
        response.raise_for_status()
        if response.headers.get("Accept-Ranges") != "bytes" or "Content-Length" not in response.headers:
            msg = f"{url} does not support range requests"
            raise RangeNotSupportedError(msg)
        self._session = session
        self._url = response.url
        self._timeout = timeout
        self._size = int(response.headers["Content-Length"])
        self._pos = 0

    def readable(self) -> bool:  # noqa: D102
        return True

    def seekable(self) -> bool:  # noqa: D102
        return True

    def tell(self) -> int:  # noqa: D102
        return self._pos

    def seek(self, offset: int, whence: int = io.SEEK_SET) -> int:  # noqa: D102
        base = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self._pos, io.SEEK_END: self._size}[whence]
        self._pos = base + offset
        return self._pos

    def readinto(self, buffer: bytearray | memoryview) -> int:  # type: ignore[override]  # noqa: D102
        if self._pos >= self._size or len(buffer) == 0:
            return 0
        end = min(self._pos + len(buffer), self._size) - 1
        response = self._session.get(
            self._url,
            headers={"Range": f"bytes={self._pos}-{end}"},
            timeout=self._timeout,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        if response.status_code != requests.codes.partial_content:
            msg = f"{self._url} ignored the range request"
            raise RangeNotSupportedError(msg)
        data = response.content
        buffer[: len(data)] = data
        self._pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


class ONSPDRelease:
    """Resolves an ONSPD release and provides access to its zip."""

    def __init__(  # noqa: PLR0913
        self,
        *,
        api_url: str,
        download_dir: Path,
        logger: logging.Logger,
        item_id: str | None = None,
        timeout: float = 120,
        session: requests.Session | None = None,
        delete_on_exit: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialise.

        Args:
            api_url: ArcGIS sharing REST API base URL.
            download_dir: Directory the zip is downloaded to.
            logger: Logger for progress messages.
            item_id: Pin a specific release; the latest is used when omitted.
            timeout: HTTP read timeout in seconds.
            session: HTTP session (a retrying one is created when omitted).
            delete_on_exit: Delete the downloaded zip when the process exits.
        """
        self._api_url = api_url.rstrip("/")
        self._download_dir = download_dir
        self._logger = logger
        self._item_id = item_id
        self._timeout = timeout
        self._session = session or build_session()
        self._delete_on_exit = delete_on_exit
        self._local_zip: zipfile.ZipFile | None = None

    @cached_property
    def info(self) -> ReleaseInfo:
        """The release to load: the pinned item, or the newest ONSPD release.

        Raises:
            ONSPDError: If the release cannot be found.
        """
        if self._item_id:
            item = self._get_json(f"{self._api_url}/content/items/{self._item_id}", {"f": "json"})
        else:
            results = self._get_json(
                f"{self._api_url}/search",
                {"q": SEARCH_QUERY, "sortField": "created", "sortOrder": "desc", "num": 1, "f": "json"},
            ).get("results", [])
            if not results:
                msg = "No ONSPD release found on ArcGIS Online"
                raise ONSPDError(msg)
            item = results[0]

        info = ReleaseInfo(
            item_id=item["id"],
            name=item["name"],
            title=item["title"],
            modified_at=dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(item["modified"] / 1000, tz=dt.timezone.utc),
        )
        self._logger.info("ONSPD release: %s (item %s, modified %s)", info.title, info.item_id, info.modified_at)
        return info

    @property
    def download_url(self) -> str:
        """URL of the release zip."""
        return f"{self._api_url}/content/items/{self.info.item_id}/data"

    @property
    def local_path(self) -> Path:
        """Where the release zip is (or will be) saved."""
        return self._download_dir / self.info.name

    @cached_property
    def remote_zip(self) -> zipfile.ZipFile:
        """The release zip, read remotely with range requests (for discovery).

        Falls back to the downloaded zip when the server does not support ranges.
        """
        try:
            raw = HttpRangeFile(self._session, self.download_url, self._timeout)
        except RangeNotSupportedError:
            self._logger.warning("Range requests not supported; downloading the full zip for discovery")
            return self.local_zip()
        return zipfile.ZipFile(io.BufferedReader(raw, buffer_size=RANGE_BUFFER_SIZE))

    def local_zip(self) -> zipfile.ZipFile:
        """Download the release zip (if needed) and open it.

        Returns:
            The open zip file.
        """
        if self._local_zip is None:
            self.download()
            self._local_zip = zipfile.ZipFile(self.local_path)
            # The SDK has no hook after the last stream syncs (Tap.sync_all is final),
            # so the zip is removed when the tap process exits.
            if self._delete_on_exit:
                atexit.register(self.cleanup)
        return self._local_zip

    def download(self) -> Path:
        """Download the release zip to ``download_dir``, resuming partial downloads.

        The file is streamed in chunks to ``<name>.part`` and renamed once it is
        complete and valid, so a zip under its final name is always usable. An
        existing valid zip is reused.

        Returns:
            Path to the downloaded zip.

        Raises:
            ONSPDError: If the download is incomplete or not a valid zip.
        """
        target = self.local_path
        size = self._remote_size()
        # ONS occasionally republishes a release under the same name, so the size must match too.
        if target.exists() and target.stat().st_size == size and zipfile.is_zipfile(target):
            self._logger.info("Using cached ONSPD zip %s", target)
            return target

        self._download_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        part = target.with_name(f"{target.name}.part")
        self._logger.info("Downloading %s (%.0f MB) to %s", self.info.name, size / 1e6, target)

        for attempt in range(1, MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            try:
                self._download_to(part, size)
                break
            except (requests.ConnectionError, requests.Timeout, requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError) as exc:
                if attempt == MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS:
                    raise
                wait = min(2**attempt, 60)
                self._logger.warning("Download interrupted (%s); resuming in %ss", exc, wait)
                time.sleep(wait)

        if part.stat().st_size != size or not zipfile.is_zipfile(part):
            msg = f"Downloaded {part} is incomplete or not a valid zip"
            raise ONSPDError(msg)
        part.replace(target)
        self._logger.info("Downloaded %s", target)
        return target

    def cleanup(self) -> None:
        """Close and delete the downloaded zip."""
        if self._local_zip is not None:
            self._local_zip.close()
            self._local_zip = None
        if self.local_path.exists():
            self.local_path.unlink()
            self._logger.info("Deleted %s", self.local_path)

    def _remote_size(self) -> int:
        response = self._session.head(self.download_url, allow_redirects=True, timeout=self._timeout)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return int(response.headers["Content-Length"])

    def _download_to(self, part: Path, size: int) -> None:
        offset = part.stat().st_size if part.exists() else 0
        if offset >= size:
            return
        headers = {"Range": f"bytes={offset}-"} if offset else {}
        with self._session.get(
            self.download_url,
            headers=headers,
            stream=True,
            timeout=(10, self._timeout),
        ) as response:
            response.raise_for_status()
            if offset and response.status_code != requests.codes.partial_content:
                self._logger.warning("Server ignored the resume request; restarting the download")
                offset = 0
            elif offset:
                self._logger.info("Resuming download at %.0f MB", offset / 1e6)

            written = offset
            next_log = 0.1
            with part.open("ab" if offset else "wb") as fh:
                for chunk in response.iter_content(CHUNK_SIZE):
                    fh.write(chunk)
                    written += len(chunk)
                    if written / size >= next_log:
                        self._logger.info("Downloaded %.0f%%", 100 * written / size)
                        next_log += 0.1

    def _get_json(self, url: str, params: dict) -> dict:
        response = self._session.get(url, params=params, timeout=self._timeout)
        response.raise_for_status()
        payload = response.json()
        # ArcGIS reports errors with HTTP 200 and an "error" object.
        if "error" in payload:
            msg = f"ArcGIS error from {url}: {payload['error']}"
            raise ONSPDError(msg)
        return payload
